texts.preamble: Achal Gupta vs The State Of U.P Thru Home Secy. Lucknow ... on 2 December, 2024 High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench ?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc-Lko:79830 Court No. - 20 Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 1349 of 2011 Applicant :- Achal Gupta Opposite Party :- The State Of U.P Thru Home Secy. Lucknow And Others Counsel for Applicant :- Chandra Shekhar Sinha Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Arvind Singh Sangwan,J. 1. This application has been filed with a prayer to quash the impugned Criminal Case No. 2455 of 2008 (Sate vs. Mohd. Saeed Ahmad and another) under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as 'Act, 1954') pending in the Court of A.C.J.M., 1st, Unnao filed by the informant who was a Food Inspector.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in paragraph No.1 of the complaint, it is stated that the informant had gone to the shop of Mohd. Saeed and found transparent polythene bag of dalmoth (edible items) without any label of the manufacturer. On oral asking, the name of the applicant surfaced as the manufacturer. 4. Learned counsel has argued that, in fact, the entire proceeding is mala fide as the petitioner is not in the business of any food article and is, in fact, having a factory of plastic molding products. Achal Gupta vs The State Of U.P Thru Home Secy. Lucknow ... on 2 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185893257/ 1 Reliance is placed upon the certificate issued by the Industries Welfare Association, Uttar Pradesh dated 22.09.2008. 5. Counsel further submits that even wife of Mohd. Saeed alias Md. Raees Ahmad from whose shop the alleged recovery was made has given an affidavit that he is not residing in India and is residing in UAE for the last so many years and on the date of incident he was not in India. 6. Counsel for the applicant submits that the prosecution of the applicant is mala fide for the reason that the informant-Food Inspector wanted some favour in purchase of the article produced by the applicant and, therefore, by mentioning that on the oral information, the name of the petitioner surfaced as manufacturer of the said food item, is not sufficient. 7. It is next argued that under Section 9-B of the Act, 1954, if some sample is found to be adulterated, the local health authorities are required to send laboratory report to the person concerned. It is submitted that no such report was sent to the applicant so as to enable him to avail his right of retesting of the second sample. 8. The counsel submits that the only reply given by the State in this regard is that the report was sent by the registered post in the year 2007 but no proof is attached. 9. In reply, learned A.G.A. for the State has raised an objection that this petition is of the year 2011 and till date, no summoning order has been passed. 10. After hearing the counsel for the parties and considering the fact that the petition is pending since 2011 and on the face of it, petitioner is able to demonstrate that he is not in the business of manufacturing any edible articles rather he is in the business of manufacturing plastic articles and secondly even the wife of Mohd. Saeed alias Raees Ahmad stated that he was not residing in India for the last so many years and also in view of the fact that in the counter affidavit no such document is annexed to show that compliance of Section 9B of Act, 1954 was made, the prosecution of the petitioner is nothing but the misuse of process of law. 11.
